title: Pico 2 Memory Map Explorer
description: A clickable vertical model of the Pico 2 address space with flash, RAM, and memory-mapped register bands, so students can classify data by region and explain why register reads differ from RAM reads.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Computer Architecture

educational.topic: Microcontroller address space and memory-mapped I/O
learningObjectives: Classify data as belonging to flash, RAM, or memory-mapped registers
Explain why reading a register differs from reading RAM
Identify which memory region a given MicroPython call reads
prerequisites: A program is stored as a file before it runs

controls.label: Any band or sub-block
controls.purpose: Open the full definition, example, and volatility

controls.label: machine.unique_id()
controls.purpose: Highlight the Unique Device ID register

assumptions: Band heights are illustrative, not proportional to real region sizes
limitations: Shows no numeric addresses or the XIP cache; the full RP2350 map has many more peripheral blocks than the four shown

keyQuestions: Which regions survive a power cycle?
Why does the volatile/non-volatile question not apply to registers?
commonMisconceptions: That a register address stores a value the way a RAM address does
That everything reachable by an address is storage
assessmentOpportunities: Classify a sample buffer, a saved file, and a GPIO pin state into the correct bands
